title: Session handshake & token rollover scratchpad
content:
Notes to self: rough guardrails for a compact session handshake and token rollover flow that works across hosted and private deployments. Goal: minimize additional RTTs for session setup, ensure safe token rollover without losing in-flight KV cache state, and give lightweight ops visibility for expirations.

High-level goals:
- Single HTTP/HTTP2/GRPC call to establish a usable session token for short-lived client connections (target latency < 20ms extra)
- Support mid-session token rollover (refresh) without requiring a full reconnect or KV cache invalidation
- Backward compatible with older clients: negotiate optional features via version and capability bits
- Make audit/tracing hooks explicit (trace_id + token id) for postmortem and billing correlation

Assumptions:
- Clients already have a long-lived API key or OIDC token (Auth-layer precondition). This protocol issues ephemeral session tokens scoped to a model/route and max-ttl.
- Server maintains per-session metadata: model_variant, pinned_cache_key, allowed_routes, creation_ts, expiry_ts, token_rotation_window.
- KV cache for autoregressive LLM is server-side; we want to preserve cache across token refresh for the same logical session.

Sketch: handshake flow (ASCII timeline)

Client                       Server                     TokenService / KMS
  |                            |                                |
  |-- POST /session/init ----->| verify API key, check quotas  |
  |                            |---> issue ephemeral token ------>|
  |                            |<--- token (id, mac, ttl) -------|
  |<-- 200 {token, sess_id} ---|                                |
  |-- Stream/Request with token ------------------------------->| use token, attach trace_id

Key fields in the initial response (text JSON example):
{
  "session_id": "sess_01E9X...",
  "token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "token_id": "tk_42Z",
  "expires_at": "2025-03-01T12:34:56Z",
  "capabilities": ["stream", "kv_cache_preserve"]
}

Version & capabilities negotiation:
- client sends optional header: X-Session-Client: {"version":"v2.1","capabilities":["rolling_refresh","prefer_h2"]} as compact JSON or base64-encoded.
- server responds with negotiated_capabilities in initial response.
- Capability bits: rolling_refresh, kv_cache_preserve, delegation, audit_context, compressed_metadata.

Token rollover modes (sketch):
1) Transparent rollover (preferred):
   - Server issues a new token before the old one expires and returns a ROLLOVER notification on the existing stream (if streaming).
   - Client swaps tokens under the hood for the next request without reconnecting.
   - Server maps token_id -> session_id; token ownership is event-sourced so both token ids are valid for a short overlap window (configurable, e.g., 30s).
   - KV cache pinned by session_id, not token_id.

2) Client-initiated refresh:
   - Client calls /session/refresh with current token. Server validates and returns new token.
   - No change to session_id. If refresh fails, client can fall back to full init.

3) Forced rollover (ops/admin):
   - Admin can revoke token id or force-rotate session. On revocation, server emits a Revoke event; in-flight requests with revoked token are completed but subsequent requests are denied.

State machine (textual):
- INIT -> ACTIVE (after token issued)
- ACTIVE -> ROLLING (server started overlapping new token)
- ROLLING -> ACTIVE (old token invalidated after overlap window)
- ACTIVE -> EXPIRED (token TTL passed)
- EXPIRED -> TERMINATED (session cleanup)

Security considerations:
- Token format: compact signed JWT-like blob, but avoid full JWT overhead. Example: base64(header).base64(payload).sig, where payload has token_id, sess_id, exp, caps. Keep signing keys rotated via KMS.
- Token minimum entropy + MAC to detect tampering. Consider symmetric MAC with KMS-managed key for speed on hot path.
- Short TTL (default 5m) for ephemeral tokens; allow client opt-in for longer under dedicated/private contracts.
- Audit: emit token_id + session_id + action events to event-log for each create/refresh/revoke. Tie to billing traces.
- Replay: require nonce or one-time-use for some ops (sensitive admin calls). Normal generation/requests are idempotent-safe.

Edge cases and questions (TODO / unresolved):
- How to ensure seamless KV cache preservation when session is moved between hosts (multi-instance serving)? We need session metadata persisted in a shared metadata store (etcd/consistent KV) but reading that on hot path may cost latency. Potential: keep metadata in a compact cookie in token payload (signed) with a host affinity hint; if mismatch, server migrates cache pointer asynchronously.
- Overlap window tradeoff: longer overlap reduces failed requests during rollover but increases attack surface. Default 30s seems ok but we should validate under load.
- Streaming: if server pushes ROLLOVER notification on existing stream, ensure clients can accept mid-stream control events. Might need a control channel prefix (e.g., event:control type:rollover token:...).

Operational UX ideas:
- Admin console view: show active sessions, token age, client IP, model_variant, ttl, and option to force-rotate or extend.
- Metrics to emit: sessions_created, sessions_refreshed, tokens_issued, tokens_revoked, avg_rollover_latency, failed_refresh_count.
- Alerts: high refresh failure rate (>1% over 5m) or sudden spike in tokens_revoked by admin.

Compatibility notes:
- Older clients (v1) will ignore capability bits; server should accept v1 clients but deny features like rolling_refresh. Provide a header Warnings: Deprecated-Client if v1 connects.

Sample control event payloads (text):
- ROLLOVER: {"type":"rollover","new_token_id":"tk_99X","overlap_seconds":30}
- REVOKE: {"type":"revoke","token_id":"tk_42Z","reason":"admin_rotate"}

Testing checklist:
- Unit tests for token parsing, overlap window enforcement, and session-state transitions.
- Integration test simulating: stream open -> server-initiated rollover -> client continues sending messages -> ensure no requests rejected.
- Chaos test: revoke token mid-stream and assert in-flight requests complete but new requests fail.
- Load test: 100k sessions with staggered TTLs and verify rollover events per second remain under target CPU.

Implementation notes (quick):
- API endpoints: /session/init, /session/refresh, /session/terminate, /session/admin/revoke. Keep POST for all mutating ops.
- Use a light in-memory LRU for session metadata on each serving host; a compact persistent backing (rocksdb or redis) for migrations.
- Token verification fast-path: check local signing key cache; fallback to KMS only on key id miss.

Next steps (short):
- Draft server proto messages for v2 handshake (compact, experimental).
- Sync with SDK team (Maya) on client-side refresh helper primitives.
- Add simple control-event wireframe to streaming protocol (ops + infra review).

Open questions to bring to sync:
- Should session_id be UUID vs monotonic counter? (UUID preferred for cross-host uniqueness)
- Max simultaneous overlapping tokens per session? (1 overlapping new token seems enough)
- Default TTL for dedicated customers vs hosted free tier?

Notes-to-self: keep this minimal and iterate. When prototyping, prefer explicit logs and metric tags to make debugging rollovers easy.

---- END OF SCRATCHPAD ----
